name: Free disk space
summary: Removes old temporary files and package-manager download caches, and on Windows cleans up superseded components, then reports how much space it freed.
risk_note: Only temporary files older than the age you choose and caches the system re-creates are removed. A program that keeps a file in a temp directory for longer than that loses it. Windows component cleanup can take a long time and uses disk and CPU while it runs; it keeps the ability to uninstall installed updates.

windows: Deletes files older than the chosen age from the Windows temp directory and from every local profile's AppData\Local\Temp; files in use are skipped, and links are never followed.
Clears the Delivery Optimization cache (peer-to-peer update downloads) where the cmdlet exists.
Runs DISM /StartComponentCleanup to remove superseded components from the component store, if that option is on. It does not use /ResetBase, so installed updates can still be uninstalled.
linux: Empties the package manager's download cache: apt-get clean, dnf/yum clean packages or zypper clean, whichever is present. Metadata and installed packages are untouched.

Deletes regular files older than the chosen age (neither modified nor read since) from /tmp and /var/tmp, staying on their file system; services' private temp directories, snap's and X server lock files are left alone.
darwin: Deletes regular files older than the chosen age from /private/tmp, /private/var/tmp and each user's ~/Library/Caches. Applications re-create their caches.
Deletes old downloads from Homebrew's cache, if Homebrew is installed. Installed formulae and casks are untouched.

parameters.name: component_cleanup
parameters.label: Clean up the Windows component store (Windows only)
